messages:
liam: FYI queue depth for ember-6b in eu-west-2 just crossed 1.2k, pslots exhausted and latency climbing. seeing sustained churn ~8k reqs/min. :rotating_light:
infra-bot: alert: model_queue_depth>1000 for ember-6b @ eu-west-2, span=5m, avg_latency=420ms, 95p=1.1s
maya: Oof. Any single-tenant spikes or is this multi-customer?
liam: multiple customers, but one big job (acme) is dominating ~45% of inflight requests.
tom: Can we temporarily reduce concurrency for ember-6b or shed low-priority routes? current fairshare seems too permissive.
sara: +1. We can change admission_control per-model weight quickly. Suggest drop model_concurrency from 64 -> 24 for ember-6b and bump fallback to ember-3b.
ops-oncall: I can flip a canary policy on a few p-slots in eu-west-2, and reroute low-tier traffic to eu-west-1. Will need approval for cross-region fallback.
liam: approve reroute for low-tier (non-dedicated) only. leave dedicated customers pinned.
maya: For short-term, also enable prefix-KV caching for acme if their workload is repeatable. Saves tokens and reduces runtime.
tom: Cost note: moving 30% to eu-west-1 will add ~12% egress + inter-region infra cost. ops-oncall ok with that for 2-3 hours?
ops-oncall: yep. will monitor spend tag "emergency_reroute".
liam: infra-bot, can you post current pslot utilization + per-model inflight?
infra-bot: pslot_util: eu-west-2: 98% (gpu-pods=124/126), model_inflight_top5: ember-6b=1204, ember-3b=312, atlas-2b=180, redwood-slim=98, custom-acme=600
sara: Quick config snippet to reduce concurrency (will roll canary 10% nodes first):
```
model: ember-6b
admission_control:
  max_concurrency: 24
  priority_cutoff: low=0.6, high=1.0
fallback:
  - model: ember-3b
    policy: prefer-region-same
```
liam: roll that canary. also add a temporary route that drops heavy ACME non-urgent batch requests older than 30s.
tom: How about preemptible scale-up? We have ~40 spare preemptible GPUs in apac that could be warmed but start time ~6m. Might be too slow.
maya: Preemptible is fine if we use them for background rebuilds, not interactive. For user-visible latency we should prefer reroute + shedding.
ops-oncall: executing canary now on 12 nodes (10%). will report back in 2m.
infra-bot: canary_update: ember-6b admission_control max_concurrency=24 on 12 nodes -> success.
ops-oncall: seeing inflight drop ~18% in canary shards, overall queue depth down 15% after redirect started. 95p latency back to ~750ms.
liam: good. keep monitoring 30m. postmortem action: add pre-configured emergency-handoff runbook and a cheaper fallback model variant for each large model.
maya: i'll draft the runbook and include cost thresholds + alert remediations.
tom: also recommend automated short-lived reprioritization based on per-customer budget tags. can prototype next sprint.
liam: thanks team. leaving ops-oncall to finish reroute and revert if noise grows. :thumbsup:
